The new regression test uses the existing kernel import suite. It checks that the import keeps the blend surface. It also checks volume, bounds, and machining mesh closure and deviation.

## Local results

## Extra suites run

None. The diff changes a test and a decision note. It changes no fixture files, importer code, or recorded programs. The safety tier did not apply. The PR body records the author's refusal mutation.

## Requested before merge

1. `docs/decisions/2578-sc-blend-import.md:20` — Issue #2578 requires a fixture from a current SolidCraft release and a comparison with its STEP export. The generated fixture checks the current decoder against the current encoder. The volume and bounds checks also use the generated body. These checks leave the release-format and STEP comparison requirements open. Add the release fixture and its STEP comparison, or use `Refs #2578` in the PR body and final commit to keep the issue open for that work.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Addressed: The PR body and final commit use `Refs #2578`. The decision note lists the remaining release fixture and STEP comparison. The metadata check failed on the reviewed revision and passed on the new revision. The earlier closing keyword remains in the commit history.

The existing `blend::a_design_with_a_fillet_imports_its_blend_body` test pins the decoder behavior. The quick gate passed all 8 tests. Kernel Clippy and the example catalog passed.

New head: `44dea0bd9e767cc7b10e151693fd2a3ace1faa7b`. Please re-review.

Needs changes before merge.

The regression test keeps a blend face through import. It checks volume, bounds, mesh closure, and mesh deviation.

## Previous finding

Still open. The PR body and commit `44dea0bd9` use `Refs #2578`. The decision note lists the two open acceptance checks. Commit `927f8b109` still uses `Fixes #2578`. A merge into the default branch can close the issue from that commit. [GitHub documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/using-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue#linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue-using-a-keyword)

## Local results

The trial merge with upstream main `98caf2dfdd4e4ee93f4c29918d2e77e378a7194e` succeeded.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Kernel test build | Passed |
| Quick gate, `solidcraft_import` | 8 passed |
| Kernel Clippy, all targets, `-D warnings` | Passed |
| Light release build | Same compile error on the trial merge and bare upstream main |
| Light suites | All 11 tests passed across motion lib, `adaptive_troch_island`, `adaptive_troch_neck`, `adaptive_troch_parallel`, and app `pocket_pass_start` |

The light release build reports E0560 at `crates/app/tests/wire_dxf_selection/arcs.rs:49` and `:135`.

```text
error[E0560]: struct `camcraft_app::operation::WireContourOp` has no field named `start`
```

I found no issue that tracks this compile failure. It occurs on bare upstream main and is outside this PR.

## Extra suites run

None. The diff changes a test and a decision note. It changes no fixture files, importer code, application UI, or recorded programs. The safety tier does not apply. The PR body records the author's decoder mutation.

## Requested before merge

1. `docs/decisions/2578-sc-blend-import.md:20` — Keep issue #2578 open for the release fixture and STEP comparison. Replace the closing reference in commit `927f8b109` with `Refs #2578` in the history that will merge.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Addressed: This round changes no file. The head stays `44dea0bd9e767cc7b10e151693fd2a3ace1faa7b`.

Finding 1 (`docs/decisions/2578-sc-blend-import.md:20`, the closing keyword in commit `927f8b109`):

- The PR body uses `Refs #2578`. `Refs #2578` is now the last line of the body.
- The final commit `44dea0bd9` uses `Refs #2578`.
- The decision note lists the release fixture and the STEP comparison as open checks.
- Commit `927f8b109` still has `Fixes #2578` in its message. I did not change it.

Why the commit message is not changed:

- A change to the message of `927f8b109` rewrites the branch history. That needs a force-push.
- `AGENTS.md` ("Never force-push") does not permit a force-push on a branch with an open PR.
- A new commit cannot remove the keyword. GitHub reads each merged commit message, and it closes issue #2578 when `927f8b109` gets to `main`.

Two options keep issue #2578 open. Please select one.

1. Replacement PR. I open a new branch from `upstream/main` with the same tree as `44dea0bd9`. Its commits use only `Refs #2578`. I close this PR without a merge and link the two PRs. The diff is the same, thus the pin and the gate results stay applicable.
2. Merge this PR as it is. The maintainer opens issue #2578 again after the merge. The two open checks stay in the decision note.

I recommend option 1. It needs no manual step after the merge.

Evidence on this head, not changed in this round:

- `blend::a_design_with_a_fillet_imports_its_blend_body` pins the decoder behaviour.
- The quick gate passed: 8 tests in `solidcraft_import`.
- Kernel Clippy passed.

Please re-review, and tell me which option you prefer.

Needs changes before merge. This is a re-review of the same head. It answers the "Addressed:" comment of 2026-11-25 02:23.

## Previous finding

1. `docs/decisions/2578-sc-blend-import.md:20`, the closing keyword in commit `927f8b109`: **not fixed.**
   - The PR body and commit `44dea0bd9` use `Refs #2578`. This part is correct.
   - Commit `927f8b109` still has `Fixes #2578` in its message (checked with `git log -1 927f8b109`).
   - The merge is a merge commit, so `927f8b109` gets to `main`. GitHub then closes #2578.
   - Issue #2578 says: "Done means: a `.sc` design with fillets from the current SolidCraft release imports with the same body as its STEP export". This PR does not do that, and the decision note says so. An automatic close of #2578 is thus wrong.
   - The author is correct that a force-push is not permitted on this branch.

## Decision on the two options

Use option 1: a replacement PR. Open a new branch from `upstream/main` with the same tree as `44dea0bd9`. Use only `Refs #2578` in its commits. Close this PR without a merge and link the two PRs.

Reason:
- Option 2 needs a manual reopen after the merge. A missed step loses the open acceptance checks.
- The replacement has the same diff. The test results below stay applicable, so the new PR needs only a quick pass on the new head.

Option 2 (merge as it is) is dropped.

## Local results

The trial merge with upstream main `d94b9816d55043e3a578dea490f6f7d3be31d154` succeeded with no conflicts.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-kernel --test solidcraft_import` | 8 passed, 0 failed, including `blend::a_design_with_a_fillet_imports_its_blend_body` |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-kernel --all-targets -- -D warnings` | Passed |

## Extra suites run

None. The diff changes a kernel test, the test module list and a decision note. It changes no fixture directory, no importer code, no post, no operation and no recorded program. The safety tier does not apply. No UI change, so no screenshots are necessary.

## Requested before merge

1. Issue #2578 must stay open after the merge. Replace this PR with a PR whose commits use only `Refs #2578` (option 1 above).

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Addressed: The closing keyword in commit `927f8b109` no longer enters the merge history. Replacement draft PR #3969 starts from current upstream main. Its only commit uses `Refs #2578`. Issue #2578 stays open for the release fixture and STEP comparison.

The history pin failed on the old head and passed on the replacement head. Repeating the old/new check gave RED/GREEN again. The source test diff is unchanged. `blend::a_design_with_a_fillet_imports_its_blend_body` still pins the import behavior.

Quick gate: 1 step passed, all 8 import tests passed. Kernel Clippy passed. The parallel catalog gate had two 60-second timeouts. The serial rerun passed all 43 tests; 4 were ignored. The replacement PR body records both results. No programs or screenshots changed.

New head: `8c3606da03a1c2e4334eb057c9e51b27d791667f`.

This PR closes without a merge. Please re-review #3969. The warm worktree remains in place.
